speaker: Steve Holmes
sentence: We never saw Rites of Spring, but their record mattered to us.

speaker: arca
sentence: He had a few Björk records that were very formative in my musical heritage [and] instruction.

speaker: at-the-drive-in
sentence: If Joe Strummer made me want to be a better man, Radiohead made me want to be a better musician.
citation: Jim Ward of At the Drive-In and Sparta, choosing Radiohead's OK Computer for Spin's "5 Albums I Can't Live Without" (2026): "If Joe Strummer made me want to be a better man, Radiohead made me want to be a better musician."
note: OK Computer is 1997, after ATDI formed (1994) but before their main records; the claim is about his musicianship in general.

speaker: Stuart Murdoch of Belle and Sebastian
sentence: The Smiths were playing ‘Bigmouth Strikes Again’, and during the course of that song I became a different person.
citation: Stuart Murdoch of Belle and Sebastian, choosing The Smiths's The Queen Is Dead for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen: "during the course of that song I became a different person."

speaker: Steve Albini
sentence: My favorite bands during that era include those mentioned above, and local/regional bands that inspired me like Naked Raygun, the Effigies, the Appliances, Killdozer, Die Kreuzen, Bad Brains, the Minutemen, Scrawl, Man-Sized Action, the Blackouts, MX-80, Chrome and a bunch of overseas bands like the Birthday Party, Killing Joke, the Bishops, Dr. Feelgood, the Raincoats, Kleenex, Delta Five, Ut, Contortions, Sonic Youth, Swans, Public Image Ltd, This Heat.

speaker: Steve Albini
sentence: My favorite bands during that era include those mentioned above, and local/regional bands that inspired me like Naked Raygun, the Effigies, the Appliances, Killdozer, Die Kreuzen, Bad Brains, the Minutemen, Scrawl, Man-Sized Action, the Blackouts, MX-80, Chrome and a bunch of overseas bands like the Birthday Party, Killing Joke, the Bishops, Dr. Feelgood, the Raincoats, Kleenex, Delta Five, Ut, Contortions, Sonic Youth, Swans, Public Image Ltd, This Heat.

speaker: bikini-kill
sentence: The quality of sound was really influential for me.
citation: Kathleen Hanna, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2013): "The quality of sound was really influential for me."
note: Said of The Real Janelle EP, which she says was produced much better than Bikini Kill's records.

speaker: blonde-redhead
sentence: It was Lush and My Bloody Valentine. I went to those shows and I just remember falling apart every time. Like, “Oh my god, this is what I want to do. I want this noise.”
citation: Kazu Makino, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2023): "It was Lush and My Bloody Valentine. I went to those shows and I just remember falling apart every time. Like, 'Oh my god, this is what I want to do. I want this noise.'"

speaker: Graham Coxon
sentence: Jo [Johnson] from Huggy Bear got me into things like Pavement and Slint and a lot of other small-label punk groups from the States

speaker: Jesse Lacey to Drowned in Sound, 2009
sentence: I think for a lot of this record we were listening to stuff that we listened to when we were younger. We were listening to Superchunk, Archers Of Loaf, Polvo, Modest Mouse, and even a lot of hardcore bands that we listened to when we were younger, like Fugazi.

speaker: bright-eyes
sentence: I got really into Elliott Smith around that same period.
citation: Conor Oberst, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2020): "I got really into Elliott Smith around that same period."
note: Mid-teens, when he was writing folk-type songs; "When you’re young, it’s easy to romanticize the tortured artist kinda thing. I absolutely fell for it."

speaker: Dan Snaith to XLR8R, 2014
sentence: In some ways, it was very much influenced by what Kieran was doing, Boards of Canada, and those kind of things, but also sampling off a lot of old records and things like that.

speaker: Chan Marshall (Cat Power)
sentence: And then it was flip-flop flip-flop flip-flop flip-flop…I played that album probably 258 times that year.
citation: Chan Marshall (Cat Power), choosing Joni Mitchell's Blue, which she played constantly at 18 for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen: "I played that album probably 258 times that year."
note: marginal: heavy listening at 18, before her own music

speaker: Robin Guthrie
sentence: I liked all the early punk—Buzzcocks, the Pistols and The Clash, before it all went commercial, when Sham 69 counted as punk.

speaker: Dan Bejar of Destroyer
sentence: There’s a song or two off Poison Season where I had songs like those Court And Spark songs in mind – this comfortable jazz-led boogie rock with poetic words.
citation: Dan Bejar of Destroyer, choosing Court And Spark by Joni Mitchell for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen: "There's a song or two off Poison Season where I had songs like those Court And Spark songs in mind - this comfortable jazz-led boogie rock with poetic words."

speaker: Patterson Hood
sentence: The Clash is still probably my all time favorite rock ’n’ roll band

speaker: Ian McCulloch of Echo & the Bunnymen
sentence: Every rhythm guitar part I’ve ever played I’ve just nicked from Lou Reed, even some of the punkier stuff. There were all these punky little rhythms.
citation: Ian McCulloch of Echo & the Bunnymen, choosing The Velvet Underground & Nico by The Velvet Underground for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen: "Every rhythm guitar part I've ever played I've just nicked from Lou Reed." He adds: "When I met the right people later in life I would use the Velvets model."

speaker: Will Sergeant of Echo & the Bunnymen
sentence: And I thought, ‘right, I can kinda do that!’ And that’s when I started getting into recording, buying tape recorders and equipment, because I saw myself more as a creator than a guitarist.
citation: Will Sergeant of Echo & the Bunnymen, choosing Brian Eno's Another Green World for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen, on watching Eno with Roxy Music: "I thought, 'right, I can kinda do that!' And that's when I started getting into recording, buying tape recorders and equipment".

speaker: Jonathan Higgs of Everything Everything
sentence: But it was very shortly after we heard that that my friend got a drum kit and my brother got a guitar, and my brother had a bass, and I knew that all I had to do was pick up that bass and we had a band.
citation: Jonathan Higgs of Everything Everything, choosing Nirvana's Nevermind for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen: "it was very shortly after we heard that that my friend got a drum kit and my brother got a guitar... I knew that all I had to do was pick up that bass and we had a band"

speaker: galaxie-500
sentence: Power, Corruption, & Lies was the college record for us. We listened to it endlessly.
citation: Damon Krukowski and Naomi Yang, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2011): "Power, Corruption, & Lies was the college record for us. We listened to it endlessly."

speaker: geese
sentence: A lot of Ween, which I feel emboldened us to give more of a sense of humour to the stuff.

speaker: Dazed (reporting Grimes)
sentence: On a more positive note, Grimes gets to express her love for Burial , one of her “all-time favourite artists”, and cites the elusive London producer among artists she considers herself a descendent of ( Aphex Twin and Animal Collective included).

speaker: Bob Mould of Hüsker Dü
sentence: I was like, "I’d rather do that". Especially when you’d hear it, definitely wanna do that.
citation: Bob Mould of Hüsker Dü, choosing Ramones by Ramones for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen: after getting the first Ramones record at 16: "I was like, 'I'd rather do that'. Especially when you'd hear it, definitely wanna do that."

speaker: Michelle Zauner of Japanese Breakfast
sentence: When I started playing guitar, it was important for me to learn how to do finger-picking style because of those Elliott Smith records.
citation: Michelle Zauner of Japanese Breakfast, choosing Elliott Smith's XO for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen: "When I started playing guitar, it was important for me to learn how to do finger-picking style because of those Elliott Smith records."

speaker: Joanna Newsom
sentence: I love Donovan, Kate Bush, Leonard Cohen. Dylan, of course.

speaker: kurt-vile
sentence: Not long after he received a banjo from his father at the age of 14, Vile began releasing cassettes of his home recordings influenced by the likes of Pavement and Beck.
citation: Fender's profile of Kurt Vile (2022 page) says that as a teenager he released cassettes of home recordings "influenced by the likes of Pavement and Beck."
note: WRITER'S prose, not Vile's quote; stated plainly as fact, so at best reported tier. Pavement and Beck are named together.

speaker: James Murphy
sentence: Between the age of 13 and 16 I liked The Clash, Bowie, Echo And The Bunnymen, The Cure, The Smiths, Sisters Of Mercy, Joy Division and New Order.

speaker: liz-phair
sentence: Slanted and Enchanted felt like someone doing what I had inside my heart to do, and it was my war call.
citation: Liz Phair, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2023): "Slanted and Enchanted felt like someone doing what I had inside my heart to do, and it was my war call."
note: Was on repeat on her Walkman while she made Exile in Guyville.

speaker: Emma Anderson of Lush
sentence: I hadn’t listened to this for a while, but I wanted to put something in that influenced my early songwriting. Hüsker Dü and Dinosaur Jr. did so much, Hüsker Dü particularly.
citation: Emma Anderson of Lush, choosing Candy Apple Grey by Hüsker Dü for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen: "I wanted to put something in that influenced my early songwriting. Hüsker Dü and Dinosaur Jr. did so much, Hüsker Dü particularly."

speaker: mary-timony
sentence: That record changed the way I thought of music completely.
citation: Mary Timony, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2014): "That record changed the way I thought of music completely."

speaker: Triple R (station's description of Isaac Brock's Formative Five)
sentence: Isaac selects his Formative Five, and shares the artists and experiences that have influenced him over his music career spanning three decades, from being introduced to They Might Be Giants, Crass and The Pixies via school goth mix tapes, to his love of Pavement and Talking Heads.

speaker: mogwai
sentence: We were interested in a lot of American rock bands like Sonic Youth and Slint, as well as 70s guitar bands like the Stooges and Television.
citation: Stuart Braithwaite, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2011): "We were interested in a lot of American rock bands like Sonic Youth and Slint, as well as 70s guitar bands like the Stooges and Television."

speaker: Stephen Morris of New Order
sentence: As a drummer, Klaus Dinger was important to me: [he taught me] how to make one riff last a lifetime!
citation: Stephen Morris of New Order, choosing Neu!'s Neu! for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen: "As a drummer, Klaus Dinger was important to me: [he taught me] how to make one riff last a lifetime!"

speaker: of-montreal
sentence: I saw what was possible, like, if these guys can do it, I can too.
citation: Kevin Barnes, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2010): "I saw what was possible, like, if these guys can do it, I can too."
note: About the Elephant 6 bands in Athens; "That's where I learned that DIY approach to music making."

speaker: perfume-genius
sentence: So I decided to listen and then I became really obsessed with them and now I really do count them as an influence.

speaker: Mike Hadreas
sentence: I was driving with a friend and they put the cover of ‘Song to the Siren’ on, and it was very transformative. I’d consider that my favorite song of all time.

speaker: Adrian Utley of Portishead
sentence: I love Neil Young and this album was massive when I was a kid. It has never left me; I always had a copy around.
citation: Adrian Utley of Portishead, choosing Harvest by Neil Young for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen: "this album was massive when I was a kid. It has never left me," adding "his life is an inspiration".

speaker: pulp
sentence: I’ve tried to introduce some elements of Adrianne Lenker and Buck Meek’s approach into my parts, and I’ve even started to play Collings guitars, following their example.
citation: Mark Webber of Pulp, choosing Big Thief's Two Hands for Spin's "5 Albums I Can't Live Without" (2024): "I've tried to introduce some elements of Adrianne Lenker and Buck Meek's approach into my parts, and I've even started to play Collings guitars, following their example."
note: About Pulp's new songs (2024), after Two Hands (2019). Same quote names Lenker; see the adrianne-lenker entry.

speaker: Andy Bell of Ride
sentence: I was getting into The Cure and The Smiths at the same time and a year or so later, when I made the switch from cassettes to vinyl, this was the first Cure record I got on vinyl, Seventeen Seconds. It’s my favourite Cure album.
citation: Andy Bell of Ride, choosing Seventeen Seconds by The Cure for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen: "I was getting into The Cure and The Smiths at the same time" as a teenager, and Seventeen Seconds was the first Cure record he bought on vinyl: "The record reminds me of being a teenager."
note: Borderline: teenage fandom, no explicit 'shaped my music'.

speaker: sex-pistols
sentence: That album was definitely one of my favorite albums. Very inspirational to me. Steered me in the direction.
citation: Steve Jones of the Sex Pistols, choosing Bowie's The Rise and Fall of Ziggy Stardust for Spin's "5 Albums I Can't Live Without" (2025): "That album was definitely one of my favorite albums. Very inspirational to me. Steered me in the direction."

speaker: Neil Halstead of Slowdive
sentence: And for me it all came from hearing SAW 85-92 and wanting to try something a bit different.
citation: Neil Halstead of Slowdive, choosing Selected Ambient Works 85-92 by Aphex Twin for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen: "it all came from hearing SAW 85-92 and wanting to try something a bit different," which fed into Slowdive's Pygmalion; the record "gave me some options".

speaker: Lee Ranaldo of Sonic Youth
sentence: I love her words, I love her guitar playing and the tunings, and it’s just constant inspiration for me, especially in that very, very personal ‘writing about your own life as subject matter’ stuff.
citation: Lee Ranaldo of Sonic Youth, choosing Ladies Of The Canyon by Joni Mitchell for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen: "it's just constant inspiration for me, especially in that very, very personal 'writing about your own life as subject matter' stuff."

speaker: Lee Ranaldo of Sonic Youth
sentence: They hardly ever rehearsed and their songs were always thrown together in some way but they made this music that inspired me almost more so than anybody else at the time.
citation: Lee Ranaldo of Sonic Youth, choosing Slanted And Enchanted by Pavement for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen: "they made this music that inspired me almost more so than anybody else at the time."
note: Borderline: Pavement (1992) came after Sonic Youth formed; he says they inspired him in general, no specific work named.

speaker: sonic-youth
sentence: We were very energized by it.
citation: Lee Ranaldo, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2012): "We were very energized by it."
note: Said of the early-80s SST/American hardcore movement; "the Minutemen always represented something a little bit closer to my heart." Sonic Youth had formed in 1981.

speaker: Britt Daniel of Spoon
sentence:
Is that heavy but still pop template something that inspired Spoon?

I think so.
citation: Britt Daniel of Spoon, asked for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen whether the heavy-but-pop template of Wipers's Over the Edge inspired Spoon: "I think so."

speaker: Laetitia Sadier of Stereolab
sentence: I think the real power that hit me was in this record; the urgency and the energy of the record.
citation: Laetitia Sadier of Stereolab, choosing The Smiths by The Smiths for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen: "I think the real power that hit me was in this record; the urgency and the energy of the record," first heard as a French adolescent, adding "I'd never heard this type of songwriting before."

speaker: Michael Gira
sentence: I listened to a wide variety of music then ­ The Stooges, Suicide, Throbbing Grist"le, SPK, Cabaret Voltaire, Whitehouse, Brian Eno, Kraftwerk, No New York , Wire, Sex Pistols, Buzzcocks, Black Flag.

speaker: Michael Gira
sentence: I listened to a wide variety of music then ­ The Stooges, Suicide, Throbbing Grist"le, SPK, Cabaret Voltaire, Whitehouse, Brian Eno, Kraftwerk, No New York , Wire, Sex Pistols, Buzzcocks, Black Flag.

speaker: Michael Gira of Swans
sentence: Drake was inspirational to me in thinking about the simplicity and about creating something that has genuine power and truth in it, with very simple means, as opposed to Swans, which relied on volume.
citation: Michael Gira of Swans, choosing Pink Moon by Nick Drake for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen: "Drake was inspirational to me in thinking about the simplicity and about creating something that has genuine power and truth in it, with very simple means, as opposed to Swans, which relied on volume."

speaker: Lol Tolhurst of The Cure
sentence: I’ve actually got part of a chapter in my new book about how Joe Strummer started me on this path.
citation: Lol Tolhurst of The Cure, choosing The Clash's debut for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen: "I've actually got part of a chapter in my new book about how Joe Strummer started me on this path."

speaker: Wayne Coyne
sentence: We’ve played with them quite a few times over the last couple of years, getting to know James Murphy and hearing that music in unexpected places. I love them now.

speaker: the-national
sentence: Neil Young and Bob Dylan, those kinds of guys.

speaker: The Radio Dept. (band site)
sentence: INFLUENCES (the band's own list on its 2007 site)

speaker: The Radio Dept. (band site)
sentence: INFLUENCES (the band's own list on its 2007 site)

speaker: Johnny Marr of The Smiths
sentence: Buzzcocks influenced The Smiths massively in the way we approached our record sleeves and our choice of independent record company – because of the Buzzcocks we took on a Mancunian DIY ethic, whilst being in the charts.
citation: Johnny Marr of The Smiths, choosing Buzzcocks's Another Music In A Different Kitchen for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen: "Buzzcocks influenced The Smiths massively in the way we approached our record sleeves and our choice of independent record company"

from: ...And You Will Know Us by the Trail of Dead
speaker: Trail of Dead (ToD) to Metropolis Japan, 2019
sentence: ToD: At the time we were influenced bands who we knew like Unwound and Karp, but also bands like Sonic Youth.

speaker: Justin Trosper (Unwound)
sentence: We were into the Melvins alot and Nirvana, but more influenced by the DC punk thing happening back then and just more interesting US hardcore(husker du/black flag/mission of burma) and punk from England(wire/gang of 4/joy division).

speaker: Xandy Chelmis
sentence: I really loved The Shins, Grizzly Bear, Real Estate, Beach Fossils, and Fleet Foxes was a big one for me.

speaker: Karly Hartzman to Chasing Sundays, 2025
sentence: I remember him playing Sunny Day Real Estate, Cocteau Twins, My Bloody Valentine.

speaker: wire
sentence: We studiously ignored Joy Division because they seemed a little too derivative of us.
citation: Colin Newman, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2017): "We studiously ignored Joy Division because they seemed a little too derivative of us."

speaker: wolf-alice
sentence: Our aspirations are to follow in that kind of vein.

speaker: yeah-yeah-yeahs
sentence: I can credit him for putting the idea in my head that I could sing too, as long as I sang my heart out.
citation: Karen O, in the Observer's Soundtrack of My Life (2014): on Neutral Milk Hotel's On Avery Island, as "the record that inspired me to sing": "I can credit him for putting the idea in my head that I could sing too, as long as I sang my heart out."
